segments.he:
ו)מעשה ברבינו ז"ל שציוה לאחותו פעריל שתתגרש עם בעלה (גיסו של רבינו ז"ל) 
שהוא שוטה (ער איז אנאר) אז ער איז אנאר נארט איהם דער בע"ד אין יודשקייט איך:
segments.en:
A story concerning Rabbainu who commanded his sister Perel to divorce her husband — his brother-in-law. He said of him: "Er iz a nar" [He is a fool] — "Az er iz a nar, nart im der Ba'al Din in Yidishkeit azoy" [Being a fool, the Accuser misleads him in his Yiddishkeit in this way].

Regarding the birth of Rabbainu — it is already explained in what was recorded above how Reb Simcha was on the road and became lost, and how his wife Feiga had distress and searched for him in all she did to honor the Shabbos and could not find him. She was in very great distress. And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai came to her several times and consoled her, saying to her: "The Prosecuting Angel stretched himself at length and breadth so as not to allow the soul [of Rabbainu] to descend to this world — and I prostrated myself and wept before the Almighty until I brought it about that the soul would come into this world." And once Rashbi said to her in these exact words: "I too have need of this soul in this world." And also the Ba'al Shem Tov came to her and told her how there had been a prosecution that the soul should not descend to this world — but Rashbi had labored greatly and brought it about that the soul would descend.

As for Reb Simcha: he had been traveling with a caravan. They all became lost on the road and scattered in every direction to look for the way. Meanwhile they found the road — but he, Reb Simcha, remained alone and could not find his way. The more he walked the more lost he became, and he was in great distress. He fell asleep. Someone came and offered him an infant, and he absolutely refused — saying: "I am lost on the road and you are giving me an infant?!" They took the infant back and brought him another [from a higher spiritual level] — and again he refused. This happened seven times. On the eighth time, when he refused, they said to him: "This is already the eighth — above all the seven" — and they placed the infant with him by force and departed.

Meanwhile he woke from his sleep and saw he was near a settled place. He went there and found the town of Orchov, home of the holy Tzaddik Reb Yitzchak of Drobitech — father of the holy Reb Yechiel Michl of Zlotchov (whose greatness is well known — the Ba'al Shem Tov said of him that he possessed the soul of Rashbi). Reb Yitzchak was then near his death. Reb Simcha entered to him and Reb Yitzchak said: "Azoy az du bist shoyn da, meg ikh shoyn zayn" [Now that you are here, I may go] — for it is known that before one Tzaddik departs, another arrives; and his intention was regarding Rabbainu, who was already in the womb. Reb Simcha did not understand and asked: "Are you saying I should leave?" He answered: "No — I said: 'Now that you are here, I may go.' And already, this is the eighth time" [referring to the eight infants of the dream].

He did not understand the whole matter. And then Reb Yitzchak rebuked his son Reb Michl and said to him: "Yoh, host du zikh shoyn far vemen tsi shemen — host nit moyre? Host far dem ba'al bayis" [Now you have someone to be ashamed before — are you not afraid? You have before this householder] — and pointed to Reb Simcha — "megstu zikh shoyn shemen" [before him you may be ashamed]. And shortly thereafter Reb Yitzchak passed away.

Reb Michl his son needed to put on tefillin the following day. It became known from the scribe that Reb Yitzchak had taken the tefillin housings from him thirty days before his death and had filled them each day with his tears [placing them there, since tefillin represent the mochin [higher mind], and tears are the overflow of the mochin]. At the moment of passing, Reb Michl was greatly aroused and proclaimed before all those present, with weeping: "Zing ir zent eydus, un der toyt iz eydus, az ikh hob zikh gezegnt dem Yetzer HoRa — mer hob ikh mit im kayn gesheft nit!" [You are all witnesses, and death is a witness, that I have bid farewell to the evil inclination — I have no more dealings with him!] And there was a great arousal. Afterward the putting on of tefillin took place with great spiritual awakening. From all of this Reb Simcha was very greatly aroused. He traveled home — and then Feiga his wife conceived Rabbainu.
